record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: In ageing science, what are the fundamental causes of ageing?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Ageing is the progressive, largely universal decline in physiological function and increase in mortality risk observed in most multicellular organisms over time. Despite extensive characterization of phenotypic and molecular changes that accompany ageing (including, e.g., genomic instability, telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, stem-cell exhaustion, altered intercellular communication, deregulated nutrient sensing, and chronic inflammation), it remains unsettled whether any of these constitute root causes or are themselves downstream consequences of deeper underlying mechanisms.

Problem. Identify and justify the fundamental cause(s) of biological ageing. Specifically:
(a) Provide a precise definition of "fundamental cause" of ageing that distinguishes primary drivers from downstream hallmarks and correlates.
(b) Determine whether ageing in metazoans is driven by a single unifying mechanism or by several independent, parallel mechanisms, and characterize the causal hierarchy among the proposed drivers.
(c) Demonstrate, via experimental or theoretical evidence, that intervening on the proposed fundamental cause(s) is sufficient to slow, halt, or reverse the ageing process across tissues and species, while intervening on purely downstream hallmarks is not.
artifact.status_search_result: The fundamental cause of ageing is widely regarded as an open question in biogerontology. Multiple competing theories (programmed/evolutionary theories, damage-accumulation theories, hyperfunction theory, hallmarks-of-ageing framework) coexist without consensus, and recent reviews continue to frame "why do we age?" as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Hallmarks of Aging (Cell, López-Otín et al., updated 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Aging is driven by a set of interrelated hallmarks; the relative contribution and causal hierarchy among them remain to be fully established.
status_evidence.claim: Mainstream review acknowledges that the causal structure underlying ageing hallmarks is not fully resolved.
